Every space already sits in some section, a default one until you move it, so this both files and re-files, and reports moved false when the space is already where you want it. For a bulk sort, read each section once with list_section_items and pass the item_name it gives you: that skips the per-space lookup. Set dry_run to see which section the space would leave without writing. Needs the chat.users.sections scope.

dry_run.description: look up where the space sits without moving it

item_name.description: the space's current sidebar entry, from list_section_items. Passing it skips a lookup, which is what makes a bulk sort cost one listing per section instead of a request per space. Nothing re-checks that it belongs to space_id, so a mismatched pair files the wrong space

tools.name: move_space_to_section

dry_run.description: true when nothing was moved

from_section.description: where the space sat before, a default section when it had never been filed. Resolved before anything is written, so a dry run reports it too

item_name.description: the sidebar entry after the move; feed it back in for a bulk sort. A move renames it, so the one you passed in no longer exists

moved.description: false without an error in two cases: a dry run, and a space already in the target section

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run that would move something, the exact body; null on a real move and on a space already in place

section_name.description: the section it was asked to go to

tools.description: Pin a message in its space, so everyone in the space sees it in the pinned list. The space is taken from the message name. Pinning is visible to everyone.

dry_run.description: check the arguments without changing anything

message_name.description: the message, spaces/{space}/messages/{message}. The space is taken from it

tools.name: pin_message

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

pin_name.description: the pin's resource name; empty after a dry run

pinned.description: true only when this call pinned the message

unpinned.description: true only when this call removed a pin. False can mean the message was not pinned

tools.description: Move a section within your sidebar. Pass exactly one of sort_order (absolute, 1 and up) or relative_position (START or END). Prefer relative_position when arranging several: Google documents sort_order as inserting at that rank and shifting the rest down, but a run of absolute inserts does not settle where that implies, so build an order by moving each to START in reverse. Set dry_run to see the request body first. Needs the chat.users.sections scope.

dry_run.description: return the request body without moving anything

relative_position.description: START or END; pass this or sort_order, not both

sort_order.description: an absolute rank, 1 and up; pass this or relative_position, not both

tools.name: position_section

dry_run.description: true when nothing was moved

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact body that would have been sent; null on a real move

sort_order.description: the rank Google reports after the move, when it reports one; null after a dry run

tools.description: Remove someone from a space by their membership resource name, which list_members gives you. Check what the membership is first: a membership can name a Google Group, and removing that one removes everyone in the group from the space. list_members reports the kind. A membership that is already gone reports removed false rather than failing, so a repeat is safe; a membership you may not remove is reported as an error instead. There is no by-email shape: the People API stays silent about people the caller cannot see, so a miss would read as already gone while the person is still in the space.

dry_run.description: check the arguments without removing anyone

membership_name.description: the membership to remove, spaces/{space}/members/{member}, from list_members

tools.name: remove_member

dry_run.description: true when nobody was removed

removed.description: true when this call removed the membership; false when it was already gone, and after a dry run. Neither is an error. A membership you may not remove is reported as an error instead, so false never hides a refusal

tools.description: Delete a reaction. Pass reaction_name on its own, or message_name with emoji and user_email to look it up first. The lookup matches on the reactor's email address, so it fails rather than reporting nothing to delete when someone who reacted cannot be resolved: a silent no was the one answer it must not give. Removed false means there was no such reaction.

emoji.description: the emoji to remove; pass it with message_name and user_email

message_name.description: the message the reaction is on; pass it with emoji and user_email

reaction_name.description: the reaction to delete, from list_reactions or add_reaction. Pass this on its own

user_email.description: whose reaction to remove; pass it with message_name and emoji

tools.name: remove_reaction

reaction_name.description: the reaction that was deleted; null when the lookup found none

removed.description: false when there was no such reaction to delete, which is not an error

tools.description: Change a custom section's label. Only custom sections can be renamed; Google refuses a patch against a system one. Set dry_run to see the patch body first. Needs the chat.users.sections scope.

dry_run.description: return the patch body without applying it

section_name.description: the section to rename, users/{user}/sections/{section}, from list_sections

tools.name: rename_section

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact body that would have been sent; null otherwise

section_name.description: the section's resource name; null after a dry-run create, because Google assigns the id

tools.description: Search Google Chat message history. Two searches in one tool. Pass query and Google searches every space you can see, matching whole words; narrow it with space_id, sender_email, mentions_me, has_attachment, has_link, unread_only and a time window. Pass regex instead and this server scans one space itself, which is the only way to match a pattern or part of a word — it needs space_id, reads pages of history, and takes none of the filters. Prefer query. If cap_reached is true the answer is partial; if unparsed is non-zero it is incomplete, and saying the space is empty would be wrong.

by_relevance.description: order by relevance instead of newest first. Google has this in Developer Preview and refuses it outside that programme

created_after.description: only messages created at or after this time; RFC 3339, such as 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Strongly recommended for a regex scan: an unbounded scan of a busy space stops at the page cap and returns a partial result

created_before.description: only messages created before this time; RFC 3339. Google's search only

has_attachment.description: only messages carrying an attachment. Google's search only

has_link.description: only messages containing a hyperlink. Google's search only

limit.description: how many matches to return, 1 to 100; default 50

max_pages.description: how many pages of history a regex scan may read, 1 to 50; default 10

mentions_me.description: only messages that @-mention you. Google's search only

page_token.description: continue Google's search from a previous next_page_token

query.description: keywords for Google's own search, matched as a phrase across whole words. Quotes, backslashes and brackets are not allowed; use regex for a literal or partial-word match

regex.description: a regular expression in RE2 syntax, scanned by this server over one space rather than by Google. The only way to match a pattern or part of a word, and the slowest: it reads pages of history. Cannot be combined with query or the filters below

sender_email.description: only messages from this person. Google's search only

space_id.description: the space to search, spaces/{id}. Google's search takes every space you can see when this is omitted; a regex scan needs it

unread_only.description: only messages you have not read. Google's search only, and it needs the read-state scope as well as the message one

tools.name: search_messages

cap_reached.description: true when there is more than was returned: a scan that hit max_pages or filled the limit, or a Google search with a further page. The answer is partial, so say so

matches.description: the messages that matched, newest first

snippet.description: up to about 160 characters of the body around the first match

timestamp.description: when the message was created, RFC 3339 in UTC

next_page_token.description: pass back as page_token to continue Google's search; a regex scan has none

scanned.description: how many messages were read before filtering. Google filters upstream, so its search reports what it returned

server_side.description: true when Google ran the search, false when this server scanned one space for a pattern

unparsed.description: messages that were read but could not be searched. Non-zero means this result is INCOMPLETE, which is not the same as no matches; say so rather than reporting the space as empty

tools.description: Look someone up across the caller's Workspace directory and their own contacts, and get their email address. Each hit says which source produced it. Directory hits are remembered, so a later get_messages or list_members resolves the same person without another lookup. Use it to turn a name or a fragment of one into the email address the other tools take.

limit.description: how many to return, 1 to 100; default 10

query.description: a name or email fragment, 1 to 200 characters

sources.description: which upstreams to ask: DIRECTORY for the Workspace directory, CONTACTS for the caller's own contacts. Default asks both, which covers a Workspace account and a personal one

tools.name: search_people

display_name.description: what to call them, or null when the hit carried no name

email.description: their email address, or null when the hit carried none

source.description: DIRECTORY for a Workspace profile, CONTACTS for the caller's own contacts

user_id.description: the Chat user id, users/{id}, when the hit is a Workspace profile. Null for a personal contact, whose id does not name anyone in Chat

sources_succeeded.description: which upstreams answered. A source that was attempted but did not succeed refused, and the matches come from the rest

total_returned.description: how many matches are in people

tools.description: Search named Google Chat spaces by display name, including spaces you are not a member of. Use it to find a space to join or read; use list_spaces for the ones you are already in, and find_group_chats for a group chat, which this cannot return. Matching is by word prefix. Without admin access Google returns a single page of up to 100 and no total.

display_name.description: match spaces whose name begins with these words; matching is by word prefix, not substring, so 'eng' finds 'Engineering' but 'ing' does not. Omit to list every named space the other filters allow

external_user_allowed.description: true for spaces that admit people outside the organisation, false for those that do not; omit for both

limit.description: how many to return, 1 to 100; default 50

page_token.description: continue a previous search; Google returns a token only with admin access

use_admin_access.description: search every space in the Workspace rather than the ones you can see. Needs Workspace admin rights and the admin toolset, which is off unless GCM_TOOLSETS names it

tools.name: search_spaces

next_page_token.description: pass back as page_token for the next page; only ever set under admin access

display_name.description: what to call the space; a direct message or group chat has no name of its own, so a label is supplied

space_id.description: the space's resource name, spaces/{id}; pass this to other tools

type.description: SPACE, DIRECT_MESSAGE, GROUP_CHAT, or SPACE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED for a kind this server does not recognise

total_size.description: how many spaces matched in total, an estimate above 10000; only ever set under admin access

tools.description: Post a text message to a Chat space, a group chat or a direct message. The body is posted exactly as given: nothing is added to it, and nothing in it is rewritten. To @mention someone, put <users/their@address> in the text yourself. Pass thread_name to reply in an existing thread, which every message carries as thread_id. Set dry_run to see the request body without posting. The post carries a client-assigned id, so this server's own retries cannot leave two copies — but calling the tool again after an error can, because that is a new post. Read the space first if you are unsure. To send a file, upload it with upload_attachment first and pass the token it returns.

attachment_upload_token.description: attach a file uploaded beforehand: the upload_token from upload_attachment, for the same space. One file per message, and the token is spent once it is posted

client_message_id.description: an id you choose, so that repeating this exact call lands on the same message instead of posting a second one. Must start with 'client-', be at most 63 characters, and hold only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Set it whenever you might retry

dry_run.description: return the request body without posting; call again without it to post

reply_fallback.description: if the thread named is gone, start a new thread instead of failing. Only meaningful with thread_name; the default fails, so a reply never lands somewhere unexpected

space_id.description: the space to post in, spaces/{id}, from list_spaces or find_direct_message

text.description: the message body, 1 to 4096 characters; posted exactly as given. To @mention someone, write <users/their@address> in the text: Google resolves the address itself when the server is signed in as a person, which this one is. <users/all> mentions and notifies EVERYONE in the space, so use it only when asked to

thread_name.description: reply in this thread, spaces/{space}/threads/{thread}; omit to start a new one

tools.name: send_message

dry_run.description: true when nothing was posted

message_id.description: the new message's resource name; null after a dry run, because nothing was posted

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact body that would have been posted; null on a real post

thread_id.description: the thread it landed in; null after a dry run

tools.description: Set your own Chat presence to ACTIVE, AWAY or DO_NOT_DISTURB. Do not disturb needs an expiry — minutes or until — which Google requires and caps at a year. Other people see this, so it is worth asking before silencing someone's notifications on their behalf.

dry_run.description: check the arguments without changing anything

minutes.description: how long do-not-disturb should last. Pass this or until, and only with DO_NOT_DISTURB, which Google requires an expiry for and caps at a year

state.description: ACTIVE, AWAY or DO_NOT_DISTURB. IDLE cannot be set: Google decides it

until.description: when do-not-disturb should end, RFC 3339. Pass this or minutes

tools.name: set_availability

do_not_disturb_until.description: when do-not-disturb ends, RFC 3339 in UTC; null when you are not in it

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

state.description: ACTIVE, IDLE, AWAY, DO_NOT_DISTURB, or STATE_UNSPECIFIED for a state this server does not recognise. IDLE is Google's to report, not yours to set

status_expires.description: when the custom status lapses, RFC 3339 in UTC; null when it does not

status_text.description: the custom status beside your name, if you have one

tools.description: Set the text and emoji beside your name in Chat, or clear it. Google wants both together and refuses one without the other; a custom emoji is not accepted here, only a Unicode one. An expiry is optional, unlike do-not-disturb's. Everyone who sees you in Chat sees this.

clear.description: remove the status you have instead of setting one. Takes no other argument

dry_run.description: return the request body without changing anything

emoji.description: one Unicode emoji beside the text. Google requires it alongside the text and refuses one of your organisation's custom emoji here. Required unless clear is set

minutes.description: how long the status should last. Pass this or until; leave both out and it stays until you change it

text.description: what the status says, up to 64 characters. Required unless clear is set

until.description: when the status should lapse, RFC 3339. Pass this or minutes

tools.name: set_custom_status

cleared.description: true when the status was removed rather than set

do_not_disturb_until.description: when do-not-disturb ends, RFC 3339 in UTC; null when you are not in it

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact body that would have been sent; null otherwise

state.description: ACTIVE, IDLE, AWAY, DO_NOT_DISTURB, or STATE_UNSPECIFIED for a state this server does not recognise. IDLE is Google's to report, not yours to set

status_expires.description: when the custom status lapses, RFC 3339 in UTC; null when it does not

status_text.description: the custom status beside your name, if you have one

tools.description: Remove a message's pin. Takes the message, not the pin: Google gives a pin the message's own id. A message that was not pinned reports unpinned false rather than failing.

dry_run.description: check the arguments without changing anything

message_name.description: the message, spaces/{space}/messages/{message}. The space is taken from it

tools.name: unpin_message

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

pin_name.description: the pin's resource name; empty after a dry run

pinned.description: true only when this call pinned the message

unpinned.description: true only when this call removed a pin. False can mean the message was not pinned

tools.description: Change what someone may do in a space: MEMBER, MANAGER or ASSISTANT_MANAGER. A manager can change the space's settings and remove people, so promoting someone gives away control of the space and demoting the last manager may leave nobody able to administer it. Role is the only thing this changes. Set dry_run to see the request body without sending it.

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact body that would have been sent; null on a real change

role.description: the role Google recorded, in its own spelling; after a dry run, the role that was asked for

tools.description: Replace the text of a message you sent. Text only: cards and attachments are left untouched, and editing them needs an identity this server does not have. Set dry_run to see the patch body without applying it. Needs the restricted-tier chat.messages scope.

dry_run.description: return the patch body without applying it

message_name.description: the message to edit, spaces/{space}/messages/{message}; you must be its sender

tools.name: update_message

dry_run.description: true when nothing was changed

rendered_payload.description: on a dry run, the exact patch body; null on a real edit

tools.description: Rename a space or change its description. Pass at least one of the two; an empty edit is refused. Editing the description clears the space's guidelines, because Google's mask covers both at once, so edit a space that has guidelines in the Chat interface instead. Set dry_run to see the patch body first. Needs the restricted-tier chat.spaces scope.

description.description: a new description, up to 150 characters; omit to leave it alone. Pass an empty string to clear it

display_name.description: a new name, 1 to 128 characters; omit to leave it alone

dry_run.description: return the patch body and its mask without applying them

tools.name: update_space

display_name.description: the name that was set, or null when the call left it alone

tools.description: Change what Chat tells you about a space, or mute it. Pass either setting or both; whatever you leave out is left alone. Affects you and nobody else.

tools.description: Upload a local file to a Chat space and get back the token that attaches it. Post it with send_message's attachment_upload_token, in the same space; nobody sees the file until then. The file has to be inside the server's local directory, and Google's limit is 200 MB. Set dry_run to check the file and see what would be sent. This needs the server to have been started with GCM_LOCAL_DIR.
